Thompson]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsWI}} The '''1994 Wisconsin gubernatorial election''' was held on November 8, 1994. In the midst of the [[Republican Revolution]], incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governor [[Tommy Thompson]] won the election with a landslide 67% of the vote, winning a third term as Governor of Wisconsin. Thompson's share of the popular vote was the highest received by any gubernatorial candidate in Wisconsin since [[1920 Wisconsin gubernatorial election|1920]]. Thompson also won 71 of Wisconsin's 72 counties, losing only [[Menominee County, Wisconsin|Menominee County]] by 20 votes. This is the most recent gubernatorial election in which [[Dane County, Wisconsin|Dane County]] (containing Wisconsin's capital of [[Madison, Wisconsin|Madison]]), as well as [[Ashland County, Wisconsin|Ashland]], [[Bayfield County, Wisconsin|Bayfield]], and [[Douglas County, Wisconsin|Douglas]] counties, have voted for the Republican candidate. ==Primary election== The primary election was held on September 13, 1994.
